description: Demonstrates SSH banner manipulation (stripping CR/LF, setting version to 1.99) to trigger compatibility mode and potential SSH-1 fallback.
expected_patched: A patched or strictly compliant SSH-2 client will reject the banner because it does not match 'SSH-2.0-*'. It will either log a version mismatch error, refuse to connect, or ignore the compatibility flag and continue with strict SSH-2 negotiation without falling back to SSH-1.
expected_vulnerable: The client receives the modified banner 'SSH-1.99-MITM_Downgrade_PoC\r\n'. Because the version is set to 1.99 and CR/LF handling is manipulated, a vulnerable client will detect compatibility mode. It may either immediately attempt an SSH-1 key exchange (sending SSH-1 specific packets) or close the connection and automatically reconnect using the legacy SSH-1 protocol on the same port.
lead_technique: SSH Version Downgrade via Compatibility Flag Manipulation

description: Demonstrates how changing username/service mid-authentication can bypass state flushing in vulnerable SSH servers.
expected_patched: The server correctly detects the username change from 'victim_user' to 'attacker_user' and flushes all accumulated authentication state. It will either disconnect (as mandated by RFC 4252) or reject the new authentication request with SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_FAILURE (type 51), preventing any state confusion.
expected_vulnerable: The server accepts the attacker_user's password authentication even though it should have rejected it due to missing state flush. The response will be SSH_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS (type 60), indicating that the server incorrectly retained victim_user's public key challenge-response state and applied it to attacker_user's password attempt.
